title: Portrait and Confession
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found wearing clothes taken from Edmund Vasquez's own shop, the retired detective recognizes the stitching of a case he buried fifteen years ago: the disappearance of Marisol Reyes, the witness whose testimony once destroyed the town's founding family. Everyone insists Marisol is dead, but the body's pockets hold a library card Edmund issued to her only last month. As he follows her paper trail through the town's archives, he discovers she has been living in plain sight, protected by the one person sworn to arrest her — and that the inheritance at stake was never money, but evidence. In the end, Edmund must choose between handing over the proof that would convict an innocent man or burning it, and his choice forces the whole town to confess what it spent fifteen years pretending not to know.
about_author: Yara Pemberton is a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unfinished business before turning it into fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet places where the past refuses to stay filed.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Edmund Vasquez's POV. He closes up his failing bookshop on a rainy Tuesday, cataloguing the town's secrets as casually as its novels. A routine inventory reveals a gap on the shelf — clothes he never stocked, tags from his own storeroom. The emotional beat is unease disguised as order; Edmund senses something has slipped out of its place.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Sheriff Dana Okafor summons him to the riverbank: a dead man dressed in garments stolen from Edmund's back room. The sheriff wants his old instincts, not his badge. Edmund recognizes the victim as a private investigator who once worked for the Vasquez family estate. The beat is dread — the past has mailed him a summons.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with a flashback to the trial that ended his career. We learn of Marisol Reyes, the witness who vanished after testifying against the Harrow family, and how Edmund quietly closed the file rather than pursue her. Guilt surfaces; he realizes the stolen clothes were a message addressed specifically to him.

chapters.title: The Library Card
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Among the dead man's effects: a library card Edmund personally issued last month to a woman named 'M. Ruiz.' Cross-referencing signatures, he confirms it is Marisol's hand. She is alive, local, and recently in contact with the murdered investigator. Hope and fear arrive together.

chapters.title: What the Harrows Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Edmund and a brief chapter from the dead investigator's notebook. The Harrow inheritance wasn't land or money but a sealed trust containing documents — including the original statement Marisol never got to finish. Someone has been paying to keep that trust unopened for fifteen years.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Watches
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He interviews Celeste Harrow, matriarch of the fading dynasty, in her decaying mansion. She denies everything elegantly but lets slip that she knows Marisol by a name no public record contains. The beat is cat-and-mouse; two people lying beautifully to each other.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Appointments
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Reconstructing the investigator's calendar, Edmund finds three meetings in his final week: one with Celeste, one with Sheriff Okafor, and one marked only 'M.R. — final delivery.' The delivery was never made. Edmund understands the killer took it — and knows what it was.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Deputy Ray Solano's POV, first time away from Edmund. Ray has been quietly shredding old evidence for someone, believing he was protecting the department. Tonight he finds his own name on the investigator's list. Panic sets in; he decides to confess to Edmund before whoever he serves silences him too.

chapters.title: Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ray arrives at the bookshop after hours, shaking, ready to talk — and is shot through the window before he can speak. Edmund drags him into the stockroom and keeps him alive long enough to whisper two words: 'the lighthouse.' The beat is grief and fury; the killer is close enough to watch.

chapters.title: Sheriff Okafor's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Dana Okafor's POV. She suspects Edmund of withholding evidence and fears the case will destroy what's left of the town's legitimacy. Her meeting with the dead investigator resurfaces in memory: he offered to sell her the truth. She refused — or did she? Duty and doubt begin to split her down the middle.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse File
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the decommissioned lighthouse, Edmund finds a weatherproof cache: half of Marisol's original testimony, plus photographs proving the Harrow patriarch coerced witnesses in 2009. The other half is missing. Someone has been here within days. The beat is revelation shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Marisol, Alive
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, first appearance. Living under the name M. Ruiz as the town's night librarian, she has spent fifteen years curating her own archive of the case. She has been testing Edmund for weeks — the stolen clothes, the card — deciding whether he is a protector or another man paid to bury her. She chooses to trust him, barely.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Marisol and Edmund. Over one long night in the bookshop, they reconstruct the case together, and an old tenderness between them — interrupted fifteen years ago by his duty to the law — rekindles. But Marisol refuses to surface while the trust remains sealed. Love asks Edmund to break every rule he ever served.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The town archivist — Marisol's only confidant — is found drowned, staged as an accident, the missing half of the testimony gone from his safe. Edmund realizes the killer isn't protecting the Harrows' secret; he's collecting all copies of it. Whoever holds the complete file controls the inheritance.

chapters.title: Celeste Opens the Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Confronted with the archivist's death, Celeste Harrow breaks: her son Julian has been draining the trust for years, and the investigator was hired by her, not against Marisol, to verify the documents before she could finally do justice. She begs Edmund to find them before Julian does. Maternal love as complicity.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following the trust's financial trail, Edmund proves Julian forged his father's signature to keep it sealed and hired the deputy's shredding to erase the evidence chain. But the ledger also shows payments to someone inside the sheriff's office still active. The net tightens around everyone Edmund trusts.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Julian corners Marisol in the library after hours, offering her freedom in exchange for the lighthouse half of the testimony. She stalls, records him on an old dictaphone, and escapes through the archive window — but leaves behind the one clue that tells Julian exactly where she'll run next.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A storm cuts the town off; phones fail. Edmund pieces together Julian's destination — the Harrow boathouse, where the trust's physical seal will be opened at midnight by an attorney's standing instruction. Everyone converging there wants the same papers; only one of them plans to leave witnesses.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. At the boathouse, Julian holds Marisol at gunpoint demanding the file; Edmund arrives and trades himself for her; Sheriff Okafor appears — revealed as the officer on Julian's payroll, torn at last between badge and conscience. The recording plays. Julian fires; Okafor takes the bullet meant for Marisol.

chapters.title: The Sealed Trust
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With Julian arrested and Okafor bleeding but alive, the attorney opens the trust at dawn. Inside: the full testimony, the coercion photographs, and the founder's letter admitting the family fortune was built on silenced witnesses. Justice outside the law finally enters the courtroom through the front door.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Witness
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Testifying under her real name at last, Marisol finishes the sentence she began fifteen years ago. The town watches, unable to look away. Afterwards, Edmund gives her the library card back, renewed. The beat is restoration — a woman stepping out of the archive and into the light.

chapters.title: Reshelving
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Months later, the bookshop thrives on new traffic; Okafor, recovered, resigns and joins the prosecution's team; Ray Solano's confession earns him probation instead of prison. Edmund shelves a new novel titled Portrait and Confession and, for the first time in fifteen years, locks nothing. Peace, earned and alphabetized.
